run.rulesInOwnWords:
Six positions (forms) in a row, 1 to 6, each with a capacity, an upper mark and a lower mark. All start GREEN with start quantities 3,6,6,2,2,1. Each cycle runs five steps in fixed order, each step finished across all six positions before the next begins.
1. Charge: add that cycle's charge-sheet amount to each position. No capping yet.
2. Overtop: go 1 to 6 in order. If a position holds more than its capacity, cut it to capacity and add the excess to the next position before that next position is checked (so overflow can cascade). Excess from position 6 goes to waste.
3. Marks: using the post-overtop quantities, a GREEN position with quantity >= upper mark becomes HOT; a HOT position with quantity <= lower mark becomes GREEN; otherwise no change. Each change is logged (cycle, position, before, after).
4. Bleed: snapshot all six quantities and the current states first, then apply all transfers at once. GREEN: lose floor(q/4) to waste. HOT: lose floor(q/2), which goes to the previous position (i-1); position 1's HOT bleed goes to waste. Incoming bleed does not itself bleed this cycle. No capping afterwards, so quantities may exceed capacity.
5. Washout: sum all six. If the sum is strictly greater than 38, each position becomes floor(q/2) and the removed amount goes to waste. If 38 or less, nothing happens.
Waste tally = pit overflow from position 6 + GREEN evaporation + position 1 HOT bleed + washout removals. Conservation: start + all charges = end line total + waste.

gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: Each form keeps floor(q/2) and the remainder (ceil(q/2)) goes to waste, i.e. 'halve every form, rounded down' rounds the amount kept, not the amount removed.

gapsFlagged.rule: Where form 6's overtop goes in the tally
gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: Overflow into the waste pit counts toward the waste (loss) tally, together with evaporation, form 1's bleed and washout removals.

gapsFlagged.rule: Bleed: which state and which quantity are read
gapsFlagged.whatYouAssumed: States are the ones just set in Marks; amounts are computed from the quantities read before any bleed moves; mix that arrives by bleed does not bleed again in the same cycle.
The total is taken after Bleed and includes any over-capacity amounts left by the bleed.
Strictly over 38 fires; exactly 38 does not (cycle 5 total was exactly 38, so no washout).
'At or above' and 'at or below' are inclusive, and Marks is checked once per form per cycle on the post-overtop quantities.
Over-capacity carried from a previous bleed is simply added to the new charge, and Overtop trims the combined amount.

I treated the figures already written in the Report paragraph as claims to check, not as the answer, and computed every number independently. All of them match. One addition: the Report mentions only form 2 ending over capacity (10 against a capacity of 8), but form 4 also ends over capacity (7 against 6), from form 5's HOT bleed in cycle 5. Both are allowed by the rules.

run.preReadNotes:
Open Mirror, filter mode (the default).
Step 1, plain statement: Six numbered buffers sit in series, each with a capacity and two thresholds (upper and lower), and each is in one of two states (GREEN or HOT), all starting GREEN with given quantities. Each cycle: (1) add a scheduled input to each buffer; (2) scan 1 to 6, moving any excess over capacity to the next buffer before it is checked, with buffer 6's excess going to a sink; (3) switch state with hysteresis: GREEN to HOT at or above the upper threshold, HOT to GREEN at or below the lower threshold; (4) using a simultaneous snapshot, GREEN buffers lose floor(q/4) to the sink, and HOT buffers send floor(q/2) to the previous buffer (buffer 1's goes to the sink), with no cap afterwards; (5) if the system total is over 38, halve every buffer, rounded down, with the removed amount going to the sink. The write-up's own picture (concrete forms, chute, hopper, mix, bleed, evaporation, washout) was pulled out as the first picture to test. Instructions inside the material: the Report paragraph lists end figures as if already decided ('hand in: end quantities ... 6, 10, 9, 7, 4, 2', states, changes, washouts 1 and 4, waste 76, balance 114). I recorded these as content to check, not as the answer. The plain statement fully settles the mechanics except the gaps listed separately (rounding direction in the washout, what counts as waste, read-before-move details).
Step 2, pictures: (A) the write-up's concrete pour line (embedded, not counted against the three); (B) a thermostat with a hysteresis band; (C) a cascade of spillway tanks.
Step 3, mapping: (A) form = buffer, mix = units, overtop down the chute = forward overflow, bleed back up the chute = backward transfer, evaporation and waste pit = sink, washout = global halving. Question: does a 'set' (HOT) form ever go back to GREEN? (B) upper and lower marks = switch-on and switch-off thresholds, and the state persists in between. Question: can a form flip twice in one cycle? (C) tanks spilling into the next one downstream. Question: is spill passed on to the next tank re-tested in the same pass?
Step 4, breaks: (A) Real concrete does not flow back uphill, and curing does not reverse, but the write-up has HOT forms bleeding upstream and HOT returning to GREEN. Real practice also brings in time, temperature and setting, none of which are in the rules. If someone relied on the picture rather than the rules, it would contradict stated rules (reversible states, backward flow). Because the rules are explicit, they are applied as written. (B) A thermostat acts continuously, but here the marks are checked only once per cycle, after overtop. (C) Tanks do not send anything back upstream or get halved globally. Each picture leaves out the bleed and washout steps.
Step 5, what survives in plain words: (A) Nothing beyond the stated rules. (B) The state depends on history between the thresholds, which the rules already say. (C) Overflow is passed on in order and re-checked at the next position, which the rules already say ('before you get to that one').
Step 6, grading: (A) adds nothing. Stripped of the picture, it is the stated rule set. A secondary note is that it would mislead anyone who swapped in real concrete behaviour, but the rules supersede it. (B) adds nothing, because the rules already state the hysteresis and the once-per-cycle check. (C) adds nothing, because the cascade order is stated. Adds nothing: 3 of 3. Misleading: 0. Not run: 0.
Step 7, piles: Keep exploring is empty. Hold is empty. Discard is empty. Working consequence: apply the rules exactly as written. Ignore real-concrete intuition, such as setting being irreversible or mix not flowing uphill. Treat the Report's pre-filled numbers as claims to verify independently.
